newsitem.title: FRANCE: Champagne growers fight high-speed rail link.
newsitem.headline: Champagne growers fight high-speed rail link.

text.p: French champagne growers fighting plans to lay high-speed TGV rail lines near their vines have commissioned a study which shows the project could trap cold air and endanger their harvest.
France-2 television said the study used an awning 200 metres (220 yards) long, and four metres (13 feet) high, to simulate the track of the Paris-Strasbourg train,
The experts concluded after several months that the embankment built for the electric train will act as a barrier to prevent cold air from rolling down a hill and away from the vines.
Winegrowers said a temperature of minus one or two Celsius, even for only a few minutes, was enough to destroy the lucrative harvest.
A spokesman for state-owned SNCF railways said it might either reduce the height of the embankment or build openings into it to allow the cold air to pass through.
